newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-GIO targets double digit growth 96/97.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-GIO targets double digit growth 96/97.

text.p: Insurance company GIO Australia Ltd said on Tuesday it was targeting double digit growth for its non-investment business units in the year to June 30, 1997.

"I'd like to see double digit growth on the business profit but with investment markets it's a question of having the right crystal ball," GIO managing director Bill Jocelyn told Reuters in a telephone interview.
GIO earlier said its net earnings before transfer to disaster reserve fell to A$150.2 million from A$156.6 million.
The group said its slight earnings decline was due to the softer market for reinsurance and corporate insurance and continued losses for its general insurance business activities.

GIO said profits arising from household insurance, business insurance and the management of non-underwritten worker's compensation business were offset by a loss arising from a market deterioration in Australian claims experience for motor vehicle insurance.

"I don't see a real improvement in the conditions for a couple of years unless we get some decent catastrophes. The industry is just too actractive internationally - we hope to maintain earnings," Jocelyn said.
GIO's reinsurance and corporate insurance division recorded earnings of A$74.9 million in 1995/96 compared to A$102.7 million in 1994/95.
Jocelyn said GIO saw medium term strength for the Australian sharemarket and had already moved to take advantage of this.
"In terms of shareholders funds we have moved a little into the sectors we favour, but it has already happened," he said.
In terms of expansion, Jocelyn said GIO was looking to set up more subsidiaries in Asia following the establishment of investment management branch in Malaysia.
"Some more subsidiaries (in Asia) are likely, particularly in India but I can't say anything nmore than that," he said.
Asked if the company was looking at any acquisition opportunities Jocelyn said GIO was continuously looking at the question of mergers and acquisitions from both directions.
"We have an open mind to whatever comes up but we don't have any specific plans at the moment," Jocelyn said.
